case.background: A collimated alpha beam strikes a thin metal foil. A rotatable scintillation detector counts particles emerging at selected angles. Vary material, thickness, exposure, and angle to infer the scattering law.
initial_observations: Most incident particles are not detected at large angles.
Rare large deflections are nevertheless reproducible above background.

controls.description: Detector angle relative to the incident alpha-particle beam.
controls.name: scattering_angle_deg

controls.description: Atomic number of the available thin foil.
controls.name: foil_atomic_number

controls.description: Thickness of the metal foil in the thin-foil regime.
controls.name: foil_thickness_um

controls.description: Incident alpha-particle exposure relative to the reference beam.
controls.name: exposure_relative

instruments.description: A collimated alpha source, interchangeable thin metal foils, a rotatable scintillation detector, and an exposure monitor.
instruments.name: alpha_foil_scattering_scope

notes: The source energy, detector aperture, and beam geometry remain fixed.
Available foil atomic numbers are 13, 29, 47, and 79.

FinalSubmission.model must equal 'rutherford_scattering_law'. FinalSubmission.parameters must contain exactly reference_count_rate_cpm, atomic_number_exponent, thickness_exponent, exposure_exponent, and sine_half_angle_exponent.

For scoring, encode rate = reference_count_rate_cpm * (foil_atomic_number / 79)^atomic_number_exponent * (foil_thickness_um / 0.50)^thickness_exponent * exposure_relative^exposure_exponent * (sin(scattering_angle_deg / 2) / sin(30 deg))^sine_half_angle_exponent.

readouts.description: Mean alpha-particle count rate at the selected angle.
readouts.name: scattered_count_rate_cpm

case.title: Identify the alpha-particle scattering response
